exclude.name: eval-quality
exclude.reason: TEA follows eval-quality's latest published release; the lockfile records the resolved version, and the resolution floor's min-release-age-exclude allows adoption when a release is published.

package-lock.json.label: root policy: allowlist + CC-BY-4.0
package-lock.json.reason: caniuse-lite is browser-support data under an attribution licence, reached only through eslint-plugin-unicorn > core-js-compat > browserslist, so it is a lint-time dependency that no published file carries.

tolerances.reason: sharp's platform binaries are optional dependencies that only the documentation site build loads. The site is private and ships as static HTML, and LGPL-3.0-or-later binds a redistributor of the covered library, which TEA never is. The root graph carries them because docs:build runs astro from the root. Publishing the site as a package withdraws this and the gate fails.

The documentation site's mermaid renderer reaches robust-predicates through d3 > d3-delaunay > delaunator; its installed package declares Unlicense and carries a LICENSE file that dedicates the code to the public domain, which places no condition on a user or redistributor. This exception applies only while the private documentation site depends on astro-mermaid.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches big-integer; its installed package declares Unlicense and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches binaryextensions; its installed package declares Artistic-2.0 and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches editions; its installed package declares Artistic-2.0 and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches fast-sha256; its installed package declares Unlicense and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches istextorbinary; its installed package declares Artistic-2.0 and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches textextensions; its installed package declares Artistic-2.0 and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches url-template; its installed package declares BSD and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

The promptfoo devDependency reaches version-range; its installed package declares Artistic-2.0 and carries a LICENSE file with that text. This exception applies only while promptfoo is the floating devDependency.

externals.rule: engine.js is the tea-evaluate runtime's one door to the optional eval-quality peer (the library, its adapters subpath, its conformance subpath for the probe parsers, and the synchronous reading of the schema-version constants and `parseAddress`); reaching any other external module here would be new, unreviewed surface on the one file the purity block holds to staying synchronous

cli/ ships in the published package and runs in an adopter's project, so it reaches only what TeA's own dependencies provide (ajv, commander, glob, js-yaml, markdown-it, minimatch, smol-toml), and Node builtins; the optional eval-quality peer is reached only through cli/lib/evaluate/engine.js, its own layer above; an evaluation framework's code belongs in an adopter's evaluator/ folder and is refused here

layers.label: the Evaluate skill's adopter evaluator templates

externals.rule: the evaluator templates run from the adopter's evaluator/ folder, with AgentEvals installed by the adopter; they use Node builtins for local observations, hashing, references and promptfoo CLI execution, while cli/ remains framework-neutral

externals.rule: the HTTP port templates are adopter code rendered into an evaluation folder's adapter/, which resolves eval-quality and TeA's host from that folder's own install (AD-20); they reach the engine, its conformance subpath, TeA's host by the package's name and Node's network builtins, and nothing else, so no template grows a dependency an adopter's install lacks

the generated hook must run in a target project that has installed nothing (tea-enforce.cjs's own documented invariant), so it may reach only Node's own builtins and nothing an npm install would need to satisfy

the site's own helpers, which tools/build-docs.js shares with the Astro config so both resolve one site URL; they reach no package, since the docs build loads them from the repository root, outside the website's own node_modules

purity.awaitRule: cli/lib/evaluate/engine.js holds the one synchronous reading of eval-quality's schema-version constants, which record builders called from synchronous code stamp from, and returns its loaders' promises without awaiting them; test/docs/eval-quality-command-adapter.md documents the invariant and an await here would break it
purity.asyncFunctionRule: cli/lib/evaluate/engine.js holds the one synchronous reading of eval-quality's schema-version constants, which record builders called from synchronous code stamp from, and returns its loaders' promises without awaiting them; test/docs/eval-quality-command-adapter.md documents the invariant and an async function here would break it
purity.newDateRule: cli/lib/evaluate/engine.js holds the one synchronous reading of eval-quality's schema-version constants, which record builders called from synchronous code stamp from, and returns its loaders' promises without awaiting them; test/docs/eval-quality-command-adapter.md documents the invariant and new Date here would break it

doc-claims-omitted-classes.$comment: Not read by any gate; each gate reads only its own top-level key, so this is a place to record a deliberate non-adoption without it being validated as part of the doc-claims section itself.
doc-claims-omitted-classes.citations: Deliberately unadopted. Eight path:line-shaped strings exist in the scanned pages today (docs/how-to/workflows/run-test-review.md and run-trace.md's worked examples, e.g. `tests/e2e/checkout.spec.ts:45`), but every one names a fixture file in the hypothetical user project those walkthroughs describe, not a line in TEA's own cli/, tools/, or test/lib/ sources this class would resolve citations against; none is a real citation into this repository's code, so the class's own refusal rule (a class examining zero real citations fails to load) still blocks adopting it as configured today. A citation naming TEA's own source added to a page later is invisible to this gate until someone notices and configures the class for real.
doc-claims-omitted-classes.vocabulary: Deliberately unadopted. Every candidate accept/refuse pair found needs either a custom verbs.accepts/refuses list or reworded prose to produce a real accept/refuse-governed sentence under the gate's verb-governance heuristic, and configuring one on a guess is exactly the false-green risk this gate exists to avoid.
doc-claims-omitted-classes.transcriptions: Deliberately unadopted. Every STRONG candidate found is either a bare number (doc-counts territory, already adopted) or a fenced bash-invocation block (doc-invocations territory, Story 4.3), not a byte-for-byte literal string block TEA's own code emits.
